title: Reduced-fibre theorem after a separable alteration of an integral base
statement: Let $S$ be an integral quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}k(S)$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Quasi-compact quasi-separated means that $S$ has a finite affine open covering whose pairwise intersections are quasi-compact. Let $f:X\to S$ be a dominant finitely presented morphism [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; dominant means that its image is dense. Suppose its generic fibre $X_\eta$ is geometrically reduced, meaning that $X_\eta\times_{k(S)}\Omega$ is reduced for every field extension $\Omega/k(S)$ [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Then there are an integral scheme $S\prime$, a proper surjective morphism $r:S\prime\to S$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] whose generic fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}L$ for a finite separable extension $L/k(S)$, and a finite morphism $q:Y\prime\to X\times_S S\prime$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] such that $q$ is an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}L$ and there is an open $U\subset X\times_S S\prime$ such that $U$ and $q^{-1}(U)$ are schematically dense and $q^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism [def-trf-modification]. Here an open $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense if $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective [def-trf-schematically-dense-open]. Moreover $Y\prime\to S\prime$ is flat and finitely presented [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and all its geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are reduced. No normality, Noetherianity, dimension bound, or flatness of $f$ is assumed.
